title: Arcane
body: Portainer Business Edition's Starter plan is $1,045 a year. Arcane does Docker management for free, under a BSD-3-Clause license. It's self-hosted, so running it and keeping it updated is on you, and nobody's on call when it breaks. It picked up 654 stars today, which is a lot more than it usually gets. A hundred people have worked on it, and the README says main is now the v3 version.
verdict: If you pay for Portainer Starter just to manage your own Docker hosts, you can cancel it.
other_side: Keep paying if you need a vendor to call when something breaks.

title: Dograh
body: Vapi's Core plan is $29 a month. Dograh is a voice agent platform you host yourself, and it has a visual workflow builder. The README says it's free to self-host and it starts with one Docker command. You still bring your own keys for the speech and language models, and you pay those providers yourself. If a live call breaks, you're the one fixing it. It has 72 contributors and the last commit was yesterday.
verdict: Before you move your phone lines off Vapi, put a few real calls through Dograh and see how it does.
other_side: Keep paying if your agents take customer calls and you don't have time to look after a server.

title: Hex
body:
Wispr Flow Pro costs $12 per user a month. Hex runs on your own computer. You talk, it turns that into text on the device and pastes it where your cursor is. The README says nothing leaves the computer once the speech model is downloaded the first time. It's made by the team behind opencode.

It got 198 stars today. Usually it's around 59 a day.

The project is still young and the experimental parts are in a Labs section. If something breaks, you'll probably have to sort it out yourself.
verdict: Run Hex next to Wispr Flow for a week before you cancel anything.
other_side: Keep paying if a support line matters for the day dictation breaks.

facts.description: Local voice dictation for mac, windows and linux
facts.readme_excerpt: # Hex Hex is local voice dictation for Mac, Windows and Linux. Hold a key, speak, and it pastes. ## How it works - hold the shortcut, speak, then let go - Hex transcribes on your device and pastes into whatever app you're in - the first run downloads a speech model; after that nothing leaves your machine - experimental features live in Labs, at the bottom of the sidebar ## What it does - hold the shortcut to dictate, or set Shortcut mode to Tap to start and stop with a press - the text lands at the cursor in whatever app you're in - Option-Shift-V pastes the last dictation again (Ctrl-Alt-V on Windows and Linux) - History keeps your dictations, searchable, for 7 days by default - Output runs every dictation through steps you choose (word replacements, built-in cleanups, your own scripts, an optional OpenCode rewrite), with different steps per app or website - Vocabulary is one list of names Hex should know; Whisper and Qwen3-ASR read it while transcribing, Parakeet models read it with Labs › Vocabulary help on, and the OpenCode rewrite uses it - Annotate records the screen while you draw and talk, on macOS, Linux and Windows (GNOME Wayland needs Labs › Annotate on GNOME) - an authenticated local API and the [TypeScript SDK](sdk/typescript/README.md) transcribe with the same model, for your own tools - Meetings is a macOS lab that records a call and writes the transcript Output and History:     ## Speech models Hex downloads one model the first time it runs and transcribes wit
